conflicts: Hyperfine constants of 3s 4P, 3p 4P°, 3p 4D° (14N, 15N): the original fit of Jennerich, Keiser, Tate (EPJD 40, 81, 2006) disagrees by up to a factor 2 and in sign with ab initio theory (Joensson et al., J. Phys. B 43, 115006, 2010). Carette et al. (arXiv:1005.0953) re-assign the weak lines as crossovers and obtain constants that agree with theory; these are the entries, the original values are under "alternatives". Neither set comes from a new measurement.
3s 4P1/2 and 3p 4D°1/2: Jennerich et al. themselves give two alternative assignments (see notes on the levels); Carette et al. choose the second.

Specific mass shifts 3s 4P5/2 -> 3p 4D°7/2 and -> 3p 4P°3/2, 3s 4P3/2 -> 3p 4P°1/2: Jennerich values (-2762.9(16), -2713.4(14), -2558.3(22) MHz) versus Carette re-analysis (-2746.4(18), -2746.4(17), -2579.4(68) MHz).

3p 4S°3/2 lifetime: 26.0(1.5) ns (Bengtsson 1992) and 26.2(2.0) ns (Bisceglia 2020) versus 23.3(2.3) ns (Catherinot & Sy 1979) and 29(4) ns (older value in Bengtsson Table I); NIST A values sum to a shorter lifetime (calculations: 23.3-25.5 ns).
3p 4D°7/2 lifetime: 44(2) ns (Bengtsson 1992), 43(3) ns (Copeland 1987) versus 27(3) and 53(8) ns (older values) and 37-40 ns from calculations.
3p 4P°5/2 lifetime: 55(5) ns (Bromander 1978) versus 39 ns (Desesquelles 1970) versus 31-34 ns (theory).
4s 2P lifetime: 6.2 ns (Dumont 1974) versus 8.0-8.8 ns (MCHF, MCDHF) and 18.8 ns (Hibbert 1991).
2s2p4 4P lifetime: published values range from 5.5(1.5) to 9.9(1.0) ns; entry is Berry et al. 7.0(0.2) ns.

3s-3p transition probabilities: Bridges & Wiese (2010) versus Musielok et al. (1995) agree within errors; both are 3-10 % below the NIST (Tachiev & Froese Fischer) values for the 3s 4P - 3p 4D° and 4S° lines.
Natural abundance: NIST Compositions gives 99.636(20) / 0.364(20) %, the IAEA LiveChart table gives 99.6205(247) / 0.3795(247) %.
not_found: Total 15N-14N isotope shifts of the 3s 4P - 3p 4P°/4D° lines (Jennerich et al. 2006; Cangiano et al., PRA 50, 1082, 1994; Holmes 1943): papers paywalled; only the specific-mass-shift part quoted by Carette et al. could be read (stored under "specific_mass_shift_MHz", not under isotope_shift_MHz).

N(3p 4S3/2) lifetime and quenching coefficients of Niemi, Schulz-von der Gathen, Doebele, J. Phys. D 34, 2330 (2001) and Adams & Miller, Chem. Phys. Lett. 295, 305 (1998): publisher pages blocked (bot wall), no open copy located; the value is only referred to (without number) in arXiv:2012.09438.
Direct lifetime measurements of the metastable 2D° and 2P° levels: none located; entries are derived from NIST (calculated) A values.
Hyperfine constants of 2p3 2D°, 2P°, 3s 2P, 3p 4S°, 3p 2D°, 3d levels: no measurement located.
Measured Lande g factors of excited levels: none located (only the ground-state g_J).
Precise (laser / frequency-comb) absolute transition frequencies: none located; NIST Ritz values remain the reference.
Lifetimes of the 3d, 4d, 5d, 5s, 6s (other than 6s 4P5/2), 7s levels drawn on the site: no measurement located.

Original papers behind the second-hand lifetimes and A values (Berry 1971, Dumont 1974, Bromander 1978, Musielok 1995, Bridges & Wiese 2010, ...) were not opened; values are as tabulated in arXiv:2302.00228.
Laser cooling of N: no proposal or experiment located.
notes: Level energies are NIST ASD values. Hyperfine: A, B in MHz, positive A means the larger F lies higher; 14N I=1, 15N I=1/2 (no B). The excited-state hyperfine constants are a re-analysis (Carette et al. 2010) of published spectra, not a new measurement: treat their uncertainties as indicative. "specific_mass_shift_MHz" is a non-schema key holding the only isotope-shift information that could be read (see not_found). A values of the 3s-3p lines are second-hand (arc-emission experiments quoted in arXiv:2302.00228); further measured A values for 3p-3d, 3p-5s, 3s-4p lines are in Table 6 of that paper and were not transcribed. TALIF schemes: 2p3 4S°3/2 -> 3p 4S°3/2 by two photons of 206.67 nm (fluorescence 742.4/744.2/746.8 nm air), calibrated against Kr 2x204.13 nm; 2p3 4S°3/2 -> 3p 4D°7/2 by two photons of 210.8 nm (fluorescence 868 nm). Forbidden-line A values are NIST critically evaluated calculations (the cached data/nist line file does not contain them); the entries with type M1 and E2 at the same wavelength are the two multipole parts of one line. Sources were located through arXiv/DataCite, CORE, HAL, Crossref and publisher abstract pages; the web-search quota of the session was exhausted, so coverage is limited to what those indexes exposed.
